misconceptions.description: Assuming an online case transfers to a real placement unchanged because it scored well online
misconceptions.trigger: candidate copies the online activity step-for-step without naming a single placement constraint
misconceptions.feedback: Name what the placement has that the online case did not (devices, time, roster) and change the activity to fit it before you teach it.

misconceptions.description: Treating a fictional online roster as if it represented the access needs of real placement students
misconceptions.trigger: candidate ignores IEPs, language needs, or access gaps that the fictional case never modeled
misconceptions.feedback: Compare the fictional roster to your real roster and let the accommodations the case ignored drive the redesign.

misconceptions.description: Accepting AI-invented class size, device access, or student names as the real placement context
misconceptions.trigger: candidate keeps AI-generated placement facts without checking them against observation
misconceptions.feedback: Treat AI context as a draft. Replace every invented fact with what you actually observed in the placement.

misconceptions.description: Citing the online module grade as proof that the adaptation worked with real students
misconceptions.trigger: candidate offers only the original score, timing, or enjoyment as evidence of fit
misconceptions.feedback: Show the assumption, the observed constraint, the change, and what students did differently. A grade is not field evidence.
